title: WPMS/1874/2013 of Harminder Singh Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 1874 (M/S) of 2013
Harminder Singh ...Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand & Others ...Respondents

Mr. Vijay Bhatt, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. K.N. Joshi, Deputy Advocate General for the State/respondent nos.1 to 3.
Mr. Pankaj Miglani, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Ashish Joshi, Advocate for
respondent no.4.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
The writ petition is listed on Restoration Application
(MCC No.242 of 2019) seeking recall of the order dated 27.02.2019,
dismissing the writ petition for want of prosecution.
2. The said Restoration Application is not seriously opposed
by the respondents and even otherwise also, the reason which has
been assigned in the application, the petitioner has satisfactorily
explained the cause of absence on 27.02.2019 when the case was
called for hearing. Thus, the order dated 27.02.2019 is recalled and
the writ petition is restored to its original number.
3. With the consent of the parties, the writ petition is taken
up for hearing on its own merits for final adjudication.
4. In the present writ petition, the petitioner has questioned
the order dated 17.05.2013 as passed by respondent no.3, by virtue of
which, the respondent had raised a demand for the payment of a sum
of Rs.5,93,424/- which was payable by the petitioner in lieu of
consideration of land under his unauthorized occupation having an
area of 183.71 sq.mts. for its conversion into a free hold rights under
the Nazul policy of the State.
5. Admittedly, the petitioner is an unauthorized occupant of
a public land lying in Mohalla Govind Pura, Subhash Nagar Road,
Tehsil Haldwani, District Nainital, and according to his own admitted
case, the petitioner happens to be an authorized occupant of the land
having an area of 183.71 sq.mts. of land for which under the Nazul

2
policy as enforced by the State Government, he had applied for
declaration of his free hold rights, after adhering to the terms and
conditions as mentioned in the Nazul policy enforced by the State
Government, by virtue of the Government Order No.407 dated
04.03.2009, there were various parameters which were provided under
the Government Order which was required to be followed prior to
declaration of free hold rights, which included the determination of
eligibility, the rates of the land which the occupant of the land was
supposed to pay the amount as determined for the purposes of
declaration of the land to be a free hold rights.
6. In the instant case so far as the petitioner is concerned,
when he had applied for seeking conversion of his free hold rights, the
District Magistrate considered the application of the petitioner as per
the norms of conversion of free hold rights and had passed an order
No.1541/25 Nazul/2012 on 07.03.2013, whereby the District
Magistrate made a declaration to the effect that the petitioner would
fall within the zone of eligibility as per the Nazul Policy of 2009, to
be considered for conversion of free hold rights. But the rider which
was attached with the letter was that the petitioner was directed to and
was also liable to deposit the conversion charges in the treasury to the
tune of Rs.5,93,424/-, which was assessed against him, and he was
directed to deposit the same, under head 0075-Miscellaneous General
Services-105 maintained by the treasury of the State, and was
supposed to produce the challan of deposit along with the Non
Judicial Stamp Paper of Rs.35,000/- by 31.03.2013, which the
petitioner failed to comply, and continued to enjoy his unauthorized
occupation of the Public Land, which was belonging to the State
occupied by him.
7. It would be relevant to refer that as per the letter of
approval for conversion issued by the District Magistrate; it did make
the liability to pay the amount referred therein, and the action which
could be taken to recover the amount by invoking clause 24 and 26 of
the Policy, itself which provides that it could be recovered as arrears
of land revenue. In an event of failure to deposit the amount thus
demanded for conversion, the circle rate of land prevailing at the

3
relevant time was to be levied on the petitioner. Thus in terms of the
Nazul policy of 2009, particularly, in accordance with Clause 24 and
26, which is quoted as under:-

8. The respondents were well within their legal duty to
recover the amount due as arrears of land revenue; due to be paid by
the petitioner, as clause 24 and 26 binds the petitioner. It
contemplated that once the respondent authorities had determined the
amount payable for declaration of a free hold rights and if the person
in whose favour declaration is to be made derelicts in remitting the
amount within the specified time frame as provided under the policy
itself, in that eventuality, the respondents would have a right under the
provisions of the policy itself to recover the said amount, which in the
instant case happens to be a sum of Rs.5,93,424/- due to be paid by
the petitioner, as arrears of land revenue. In an event of the person
favoured with conversion, there is non compliance of the provisions
contained under Clause 24, the consequential action which was
contemplated to be taken against an applicant for the declaration of
the land as free hold was provided under Clause 26.
9. In the case of the petitioner as raised in the writ petition
for the purposes of declaration of his free hold rights, the amount was
already determined as back as on 07.03.2013 and a demand to the said
effect was raised from the petitioner by the respondents through their
various letters issued by them and the report submitted in continuation
thereto. But still the amount as demanded was not satisfied,
consequently, resulting into issuing of the impugned order dated
17.05.2013, whereby, by invoking Clause 26 of the Nazul policy of
2009, it was provided that in case if the amount as demanded therein
is not remitted by the petitioner within a period of 15 days as
contemplated under Clause 26, it would be recovered as arrears of
land revenue. In that eventuality of failure to deposit the amount

4
demanded then whatsoever the amount has been deposited by the
petitioner for the conversion of the land into a free hold rights would
stand forfeited in terms of clause 26 of the Nazul policy of 2009.
10. Considering the argument as extended by the learned
counsel for the petitioner, as well as of the respondent, this Court is of
the view that once the petitioner claim for determination of his rights
of declaration of a free hold rights in relation to a land which was
admittedly unauthorizedly occupied by him and if at all he wanted to
take an advantage of the Government Order dated 01.03.2009 i.e.
Nazul policy of 2009, he would be equally bound by the terms and
conditions as contained in the Nazul policy of 2009 to discharge his
financial liabilities which related to the determination of the rates of
free hold which was to be determined in accordance with the norms as
provided in the Nazul policy of 2009, and in an event of failure to
deposit the amount as demanded for the purposes of conversion of
land into free hold the consequential action too was contemplated
under the said policy itself as referred Clause 24 and 26 of the policy
itself.
11. The impugned order which has been put to challenge by
the petitioner i.e. dated 17.05.2013, since being in consonance to the
stipulation under Clause 24 and 26 of the Nazul policy of 2009, under
which the petitioner was deriving the benefit of conversion of an
unauthorized occupation of the land of State of his free hold rights.
He would be liable to meet the demand as raised by the impugned
order dated 17.05.2013, in such an eventuality, there was no occasion
for the petitioner to challenge the impugned order dated 17.05.2013,
because it was a liability which was statutorily binding required to be
fulfilled by the petitioner for the purposes of establishment of his free
hold rights in relation to the land which belonged to the State
Government as he was being favoured with a right over an immovable
property.
12. At this stage, the petitioner contends that he is willing to
deposit the amount as demanded by the impugned order dated
17.05.2013 or as enforced in pursuance to the Nazul policy of 2009, in
such an eventuality, where a right and title is being created in relation

5
to immovable property in favour of the petitioner. He is bound to
comply with the conditions as enumerated in the impugned order
dated 17.05.2013. Consequently, this Court does not find any merit in
the writ petition and the same is hereby dismissed.
13. However, if subject to the above undertaking as
expressed by the learned counsel for the petitioner, if the petitioner
makes good the deposit as demanded by the impugned order and there
is no other legal impediment as of now within a period of 15 days
from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order. The
respondent would consider the application of the petitioner for
conversion of the land into free hold rights as claimed by him, if there
happens to be no other legal bar in granting the conversion while
considering the issue of conversion of land into a grant of free hold
rights, the authorities competent to consider will function in
accordance to the interim order passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in
Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.33695 of 2018 and the order dated
08.10.2018 as passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court on it.
14. Subject to the above observations, the present writ
petition stands dismissed.
15. However, there would be no order as to costs.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 09.04.2019
 Ravi
